title: Power Automate for desktop: flowchart mode for building and viewing desktop flows
summary: The maker controls, default state and product licensing are supported by Microsoft's documentation. The briefing accurately reports the roadmap targets alongside the documented preview and distinguishes unpublished feature-specific controls and pricing from existing product rules.

claims.claim: Flowchart mode is a visual authoring mode for desktop flows in Power Automate for desktop.
claims.quote: Flowchart mode provides a visual authoring experience in which desktop flow actions are represented as nodes and the connections between nodes are represented as edges.

claims.claim: Actions appear as nodes on a canvas.
claims.quote: Flowchart mode displays actions as connected nodes on a canvas.

claims.claim: Edges between nodes show execution paths.
claims.quote: Each action is represented as a node, and edges connect the nodes to show their execution paths.

claims.claim: Microsoft says flowchart mode can make branches, loops and complex logic easier to understand.
claims.quote: This view can make execution paths easier to understand, especially in flows that contain branches, loops, or other complex logic.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters; Governance guidance; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Sequence mode displays a numbered list and remains the default.
claims.quote: Sequence mode displays actions as a numbered list. Sequence mode is the default.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; What's changing; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: The maker path is Power Automate for desktop > Console > New flow > Create a flow > Flowchart mode (Preview).
claims.quote:
Open Power Automate for desktop.
2. In the console, select New flow.
3. In the Create a flow dialog, enter a name for the desktop flow. If you leave the field empty, a name is generated automatically.
4. Select Flowchart mode (Preview).

claims.claim: An existing flow can be opened in flowchart mode through the designer's View > Flowchart mode menu.
claims.quote:
Open the desktop flow in the designer.
2. Select View.
3. Select one of the following options:
    - To open the flow in flowchart mode, select Flowchart mode.

claims.claim: The designer's View > Sequence mode menu switches a flow back to sequence mode.
claims.quote:
Select View.
3. Select one of the following options:
    - To open the flow in flowchart mode, select Flowchart mode.
    - To open the flow in sequence mode, select Sequence mode.

claims.where: controls[0].note; What's changing; Risk assessment; Scope; Governance guidance
claims.claim: A flow must have no errors before switching to flowchart mode.
claims.quote: You can switch to flowchart mode only when the flow has no errors. If the flow contains errors, resolve them before you switch modes.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Both modes represent the same desktop flow rather than separate flows.
claims.quote: Both modes represent the same desktop flow.

claims.claim: Changes made in one mode are available in the other.
claims.quote: Changes that you make in one mode are available when you open the flow in the other mode.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; Governance guidance
claims.claim: The If action uses a consolidated properties dialog in flowchart mode.
claims.quote: In flowchart mode, the If action uses a consolidated properties dialog that contains the complete conditional structure.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; Governance guidance
claims.claim: The Switch action uses a consolidated properties dialog in flowchart mode.
claims.quote: In flowchart mode, the Switch action uses a consolidated properties dialog for the Switch expression and its cases.

claims.claim: Action-based conditions such as If process and If file exists retain their standard properties dialogs.
claims.quote: Action-based conditions, such as If process and If file exists, continue to use their standard properties dialogs.

claims.claim: Loop nodes have a loop-back edge representing the loop body.
claims.quote: A loop node has a loop-back edge that represents the loop body and an outgoing edge that continues execution after the loop finishes.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Run from here starts executing the flow at the selected action.
claims.quote: Open a node's context menu and select Run from here to run the flow starting from that action.

claims.claim: Flowchart mode uses the standard desktop flow debugging tools.
claims.quote: Use the standard desktop flow debugging tools while viewing the flow as a flowchart.

claims.claim: Flowchart mode provides a minimap.
claims.quote: The minimap displays a compact overview of the flowchart and identifies the visible area of the canvas.

claims.claim: Flowchart mode supports canvas zoom.
claims.quote: Hold Ctrl and rotate the mouse wheel to zoom in or out.

claims.claim: Flowchart mode has keyboard shortcuts for navigation and node operations.
claims.quote: The following keyboard shortcuts apply to canvas navigation and node operations in flowchart mode.

claims.claim: Adding an action from an edge inserts it before its properties dialog opens.
claims.quote: The action is added to the flow before its properties dialog opens.

claims.claim: Closing or cancelling the properties dialog does not remove the inserted action.
claims.quote: Closing or canceling the dialog doesn't remove the action from the flow.

claims.claim: Move changes only the node's visual position.
claims.quote: Moving changes only the node's position on the canvas.

claims.claim: Reorder changes the flow's execution order.
claims.quote: Reordering changes the flow's execution order.

claims.claim: Move and Reorder use different shortcuts.
claims.quote: The Ctrl+Shift+Arrow shortcuts change only the node's position on the canvas. The Shift+Alt+Arrow shortcuts change the flow's execution order.

claims.claim: Node indexes match the action indexes in sequence mode.
claims.quote: Node index badges match the action indexes you see in sequence mode.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance controls; rationale: impact
claims.claim: The change concerns how the same flow is visualized and edited rather than introducing a different runtime flow.
claims.quote:
Both modes represent the same desktop flow.
Flowchart mode changes how you visualize and edit the current subflow.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; What's changing; Scope; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Flowchart mode is user-opt-in: makers choose it per flow, with no documented automatic conversion or admin enablement prerequisite.
claims.quote: Searched: "flowchart mode" "desktop" "disable" "policy". Opened learn.microsoft.com/power-automate/desktop-flows/flowchart-flow-designer and /governance: sequence is default; makers select the new-flow option or View menu; no admin switch or automatic conversion documented.

claims.claim: An API or CLI operation to choose the desktop flow designer mode is not yet documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "flowchart" "desktop" "Dataverse" "workflow" "API" "pac". Opened learn.microsoft.com/power-automate/developer/desktop-flow-public-apis and /desktop-flows/flowchart-flow-designer; found no operation that sets the designer mode.

claims.where: controls[1]; summary; Why it matters; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: A tenant, environment or registry switch specifically allowing or blocking flowchart mode is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "flowchart mode" "desktop" "disable" "policy" and "flowchart mode" "Power Automate" admin disable registry API license pricing. Opened learn.microsoft.com/power-automate/desktop-flows/governance and /flowchart-flow-designer; no feature-specific switch found.

claims.claim: The governance page documents registry settings covering updates, sign-in, proxies, logging and copilot capabilities.
claims.quote:
Prevent users from manually updating Power Automate for desktop
Prevent user access to Power Automate for desktop with specific types of accounts
Configure Power Automate for desktop to interact with a corporate proxy server
Turn on verbose logging state in Power Automate for desktop

claims.claim: The governance page's registry restrictions can restrict access to Power Automate for desktop as a whole.
claims.quote: If all the following registry keys are set to 1, users can't sign in to Power Automate for desktop using any type of account.

claims.where: front matter: licensing; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The included licensing model refers to the existing Power Automate for desktop entitlements rather than a separately documented flowchart-mode licence.
claims.quote:
Windows 11 users can try desktop flows in attended RPA for personal productivity in the default environment.
To get full cloud flows and RPA features, purchase the Power Automate Premium plan.

claims.claim: Windows 10 and Windows Server 2016 users can use Power Automate for desktop and have usage rights for it.
claims.quote:
Can Windows 10 and Windows Server 2016 users use Power Automate for desktop?

Yes, they can use Power Automate for desktop and have usage rights for it, but they need to download it from the download center.

claims.claim: Windows 11 users can try attended desktop flows for personal productivity in the default environment.
claims.quote: Windows 11 users can try desktop flows in attended RPA for personal productivity in the default environment.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Power Automate Premium provides access to premium RPA features except unattended RPA and hosted RPA.
claims.quote: The Power Automate Premium license provides access to all RPA premium features, except unattended RPA and hosted RPA.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
